question.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\frac{x}{y+z},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ exists.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when $y+z\ne 0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y+z\ne 0\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y+z}) \\  & =-\frac{x}{(y+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{y}(x,y,z)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+z)^{2} & \ne 0 \\ y+z & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y+z\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y+z\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,y+z\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,y+z\ne 0\}.\end{aligned}
$$
